subject: Basic Medical Sciences
title: Build the biological foundations
summary: Connect homeostasis, membranes, tissue families and innate immunity.

sources.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e
sources.section: 21.2 Barrier Defenses and the Innate Immune Response

units.title: Homeostasis is dynamic regulation
units.lesson: Homeostasis maintains physiological variables within functional ranges. Negative feedback opposes a deviation rather than amplifying it. A sensor detects change, a control process compares information, and an effector produces a response. Regulation does not mean a variable never fluctuates; the response to deviation is the key concept.
units.question: What does negative feedback tend to do?
units.explanation: Negative feedback counters departure from the regulated range.
rationales: Amplification describes a different feedback pattern.

units.title: A boundary can be selective
units.lesson: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins. Hydrophilic heads face watery environments while hydrophobic tails orient inward. The membrane separates compartments and regulates exchange. Selective permeability means substances do not all cross in the same way or at the same rate; a membrane is not simply an unrestricted hole.
units.question: Which membrane region is oriented toward water?
units.explanation: Polar heads interact with the aqueous environments.
rationales: Hydrophobic tails orient away from water.
Enamel is not the membrane bilayer.

units.title: Four tissue families
units.lesson: The four broad tissue categories are epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous. Epithelium covers or lines surfaces; connective tissue supports and integrates structures; muscle contracts; nervous tissue transmits signals. An organ combines more than one tissue type. Classify by structure and function rather than assuming an entire organ contains a single family.
units.question: Which tissue category is specialized for contraction?
units.explanation: Contraction is a core muscle specialization.

units.title: Innate and adaptive responses cooperate
units.lesson: Innate immune barriers and responses provide relatively rapid protection. Adaptive responses develop specificity to particular targets and cooperate with innate mechanisms. The two are not isolated alternatives. An intact barrier is part of defence before an infection becomes established; inflammation is one component of a wider immune response.
units.question: Which description fits innate barriers?
choices: Early broad protection at body surfaces
Only the shape of a tooth crown
units.explanation: Barriers are part of early innate defence.
rationales: Exam scores are not immune mechanisms.
Crown shape is not the immune category.

units.question: A model variable rises above its regulated range and triggers a response opposing the rise. Which pattern is illustrated?
units.explanation: The response opposes the initial deviation.

units.title: A boundary can be selective · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: Which statement best expresses selective membrane permeability?
choices: All substances cross by identical routes at identical rates
Crossing depends on membrane and substance properties
No substance can ever cross a cell membrane
units.explanation: Selective exchange differs from both unrestricted and impossible passage.
rationales: This preserves the selective boundary concept.

units.question: Which pairing correctly matches a tissue family with a core function?
choices: Epithelium: contraction as its defining specialization
units.explanation: The broad tissue categories have distinct core functions.
rationales: Surface lining is an epithelial role.

units.title: Innate and adaptive responses cooperate · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: Which relationship between innate and adaptive immunity is correct?
choices: They function as completely isolated alternatives
The two terms describe identical mechanisms
They cooperate while differing in features such as specificity
units.explanation: The systems are distinct and interacting.
rationales: They influence and support one another.
This preserves both distinction and cooperation.
